sanskrit: evaṃ saptadaśaṃ dehe vṛtaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir guṇaiḥ manīṣī manasā vipraḥ paśyaty ātmānam ātmani
english: Thus, enwrapped within the body by the sixteen constituents as a seventeenth, the discerning brāhmaṇa, through the mind, beholds the Self within the self.

sanskrit: na hy ayaṃ cakṣuṣā dṛśyo na ca sarvair apīndriyaiḥ manasā saṃpradīptena mahān ātmā prakāśate
english: For this great Self is not to be seen by the eye, nor by all the senses together; only by a mind kindled bright does it shine forth.

sanskrit: aśabdasparśarūpaṃ tad arasāgandham avyayam aśarīraṃ śarīre sve nirīkṣeta nirindriyam
english: That imperishable One, without sound, touch, or form, without taste or smell, bodiless and senseless, one should behold within one's own body.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ vyaktadeheṣu martyeṣv amaram āśritam yo 'nupaśyati sa pretya kalpate brahmabhūyase
english: He who perceives the Unmanifest abiding within manifest bodies, the Deathless seated amid mortals, becomes fit, after death, for union with Brahman.

sanskrit: vidyābhijanasaṃpanne brāhmaṇe gavi hastini śuni caiva śvapāke ca paṇḍitāḥ samadarśinaḥ
english: In a brāhmaṇa endowed with learning and high birth, in a cow, in an elephant, in a dog, and in a dog-eating outcaste alike, the wise look with an equal eye.

sanskrit: sa hi sarveṣu bhūteṣu jaṅgameṣu dhruveṣu ca vasaty eko mahān ātmā yena sarvam idaṃ tatam
english: For in all beings, the moving and the unmoving, dwells that one great Self, by whom all this universe is pervaded.

sanskrit: sarvabhūteṣu cātmānaṃ sarvabhūtāni cātmani yadā paśyati bhūtātmā brahma saṃpadyate tadā
english: When the embodied soul beholds the Self in all beings and all beings within the Self, then it attains to Brahman.

sanskrit: yāvān ātmani vedātmā tāvān ātmā parātmani ya evaṃ satataṃ veda so 'mṛtatvāya kalpate
english: As far as one knows the Self within oneself, so far is the Self present in the Supreme Self; whoever knows this without ceasing becomes fit for immortality.

sanskrit: sarvabhūtātmabhūtasya sarvabhūtahitasya ca devāpi mārge muhyanti apadasya padaiṣiṇaḥ
english: As for him who has become the Self of all beings and who seeks the welfare of all, even the gods grow bewildered upon his path, searching for the footprint of one who leaves no trace.

sanskrit: śakunīnām ivākāśe jale vāricarasya vā yathā gatir na dṛśyeta tathaiva sumahātmanaḥ
english: As the path of birds through the sky, or of a creature moving through the water, cannot be seen, even so is the course of one of lofty soul.

sanskrit: kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni sarvāṇy evātmanātmani yasmiṃs tu pacyate kālas taṃ na vedeha kaś cana
english: Time ripens all beings within itself by itself; but the One in whom Time itself is ripened—him no one here can know.

sanskrit: na tad ūrdhvaṃ na tiryak ca nādho na ca tiraḥ punaḥ na madhye pratigṛhṇīte naiva kaś cit kutaś cana
english: That is not above, not across, not below, not aside, not in the middle; no one anywhere can lay hold of it from any direction.

sanskrit: sarve 'ntaḥsthā ime lokā bāhyam eṣāṃ na kiṃ cana yaḥ sahasraṃ samāgacched yathā bāṇo guṇacyutaḥ
english: All these worlds abide within it; outside them there is nothing whatever. Though an arrow sped from the bowstring should fly a thousand leagues,

sanskrit: naivāntaṃ kāraṇasyeyād yady api syān manojavaḥ tasmāt sūkṣmāt sūkṣmataraṃ nāsti sthūlataraṃ tataḥ
english: it could never reach the end of that Cause, even were it swift as thought. Finer than that subtle One there is nothing finer, nor anything grosser than it.

sanskrit: sarvataḥpāṇipādāntaṃ sarvatokṣiśiromukham sarvataḥśrutimal loke sarvam āvṛtya tiṣṭhati
english: With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads, and faces on every side, with ears on every side, it stands in the world, enveloping all.

sanskrit: tad evāṇor aṇutaraṃ tan mahadbhyo mahattaram tad antaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ dhruvaṃ tiṣṭhan na dṛśyate
english: That very One is smaller than the small, greater than the great; abiding firm within all beings, it remains unseen.

sanskrit: akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ caiva dvaidhībhāvo 'yam ātmanaḥ kṣaraḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu divyaṃ hy amṛtam akṣaram
english: The imperishable and the perishable—this is the twofold being of the Self: perishable in all creatures, but divine, deathless, and imperishable in its higher nature.

sanskrit: navadvāraṃ puraṃ gatvā haṃso hi niyato vaśī īśaḥ sarvasya bhūtasya sthāvarasya carasya ca
english: Having entered the city of nine gates, the Swan dwells there, self-controlled and master of itself—the Lord of every being, unmoving and moving alike.

sanskrit: hānibhaṅgavikalpānāṃ navānāṃ saṃśrayeṇa ca śarīrāṇām ajasyāhur haṃsatvaṃ pāradarśinaḥ
english: Because it takes shelter in successive bodies—new ones subject to loss, decay, and change—those who see to the far shore speak of the unborn One's nature as that of the Swan.

sanskrit: haṃsoktaṃ cākṣaraṃ caiva kūṭasthaṃ yat tad akṣaram tad vidvān akṣaraṃ prāpya jahāti prāṇajanmanī
english: That which is called the Swan, the Imperishable, the Immutable that stands fixed at the summit—the wise man who knows it, attaining that Imperishable, casts off both breath and birth.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca pṛcchatas tava satputra yathāvad iha tattvataḥ sāṃkhyanyāyena saṃyuktaṃ yad etat kīrtitaṃ mayā
english: Vyāsa said: To you who ask, O worthy son, I have here duly proclaimed, in its very truth, that which is bound up with the method of Sāṃkhya.

sanskrit: yogakṛtyaṃ tu te kṛtsnaṃ vartayiṣyāmi tac chṛṇu ekatvaṃ buddhimanasor indriyāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ ātmano dhyāyinas tāta jñānam etad anuttamam
english: Now I shall expound to you the whole practice of Yoga—hear it. The complete oneness of intellect, mind, and the senses for one who meditates upon the Self—this, my son, is the unsurpassed knowledge.

sanskrit: tad etad upaśāntena dāntenādhyātmaśīlinā ātmārāmeṇa buddhena boddhavyaṃ śucikarmaṇā
english: This is to be understood by one who is tranquil, self-restrained, devoted to the inner Self, taking delight in the Self, awakened, and pure in his deeds.

sanskrit: yogadoṣān samucchidya pañca yān kavayo viduḥ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca lobhaṃ ca bhayaṃ svapnaṃ ca pañcamam
english: Having wholly cut away the five faults of Yoga which the sages know—desire, anger, and greed, fear, and sleep as the fifth—

sanskrit: krodhaṃ śamena jayati kāmaṃ saṃkalpavarjanāt sattvasaṃsevanād dhīro nidrām ucchettum arhati
english: one conquers anger by calm and desire by renouncing intention; and by cultivating purity of being the steadfast man is able to root out sleep.

sanskrit: dhṛtyā śiśnodaraṃ rakṣet pāṇipādaṃ ca cakṣuṣā cakṣuḥ śrotre ca manasā mano vācaṃ ca karmaṇā
english: With firmness one should guard the loins and the belly; with the eye, the hands and feet; with the mind, the eye and the ears; and with right action, the mind and speech.

sanskrit: apramādād bhayaṃ jahyāl lobhaṃ prājñopasevanāt evam etān yogadoṣāñ jayen nityam atandritaḥ
english: By vigilance one should cast off fear, and greed by attending upon the wise; thus, ever unwearied, one should conquer these faults of Yoga.

sanskrit: agnīṃś ca brāhmaṇāṃś cārced devatāḥ praṇameta ca varjayed ruṣitāṃ vācaṃ hiṃsāyuktāṃ manonugām
english: He should honor the sacred fires and the brāhmaṇas, and bow before the gods; he should shun angry speech bound up with harm and prompted by an ill mind.

sanskrit: brahma tejomayaṃ śukraṃ yasya sarvam idaṃ rasaḥ ekasya bhūtaṃ bhūtasya dvayaṃ sthāvarajaṅgamam
english: Brahman is radiant, luminous seed, of which all this is the essence; from that one Being arose the twofold creation, the unmoving and the moving.

sanskrit: dhyānam adhyayanaṃ dānaṃ satyaṃ hrīr ārjavaṃ kṣamā śaucam āhārasaṃśuddhir indriyāṇāṃ ca nigrahaḥ
english: Meditation, study, charity, truth, modesty, uprightness, forbearance, purity, purity of diet, and the restraint of the senses—

sanskrit: etair vivardhate tejaḥ pāpmānaṃ cāpakarṣati sidhyanti cāsya sarvārthā vijñānaṃ ca pravartate
english: by these one's inner radiance increases and one's evil is drawn away; all his aims are accomplished, and true discernment unfolds.

sanskrit: samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu labdhālabdhena vartayan dhutapāpmā tu tejasvī laghvāhāro jitendriyaḥ kāmakrodhau vaśe kṛtvā ninīṣed brahmaṇaḥ padam
english: Even-minded toward all beings, faring on with whatever is gained or not gained, with his evil shaken off, radiant, of light diet, his senses mastered—having brought desire and anger under his sway, he should strive to attain the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: manasaś cendriyāṇāṃ ca kṛtvaikāgryaṃ samāhitaḥ prāg rātrāpararātreṣu dhārayen mana ātmanā
english: Having made the mind and the senses one-pointed, collected within himself, in the first watch of the night and in the last he should hold the mind steady by the self.

sanskrit: jantoḥ pañcendriyasyāsya yad ekaṃ chidram indriyam tato 'sya sravati prajñā dṛteḥ pādād ivodakam
english: In a creature endowed with the five senses, through whichever single sense is left as an opening, his wisdom leaks away, as water from the foot of a waterskin.

sanskrit: manas tu pūrvam ādadyāt kumīnān iva matsyahā tataḥ śrotraṃ tataś cakṣur jihvāṃ ghrāṇaṃ ca yogavit
english: The knower of Yoga should first draw in the mind, as a fisherman draws in the fish; then the ear, then the eye, the tongue, and the nose.

sanskrit: tata etāni saṃyamya manasi sthāpayed yatiḥ tathaivāpohya saṃkalpān mano hy ātmani dhārayet
english: Then, having reined these in, the ascetic should fix them in the mind; and likewise, having banished all intentions, he should hold the mind steady in the Self.

sanskrit: pañca jñānena saṃdhāya manasi sthāpayed yatiḥ yadaitāny avatiṣṭhante manaḥṣaṣṭhāni cātmani prasīdanti ca saṃsthāya tadā brahma prakāśate
english: Having gathered the five by knowledge, the ascetic should fix them in the mind; and when these, together with the mind as the sixth, come to rest within the Self and, abiding there, grow serene, then Brahman shines forth.

sanskrit: vidhūma iva dīptārcir āditya iva dīptimān vaidyuto 'gnir ivākāśe paśyaty ātmānam ātmanā sarvaṃ ca tatra sarvatra vyāpakatvāc ca dṛśyate
english: Like a smokeless flame burning bright, radiant as the sun, like lightning-fire in the sky, he beholds the Self by the self; and there, everywhere, by reason of its all-pervadingness, the All is seen.

sanskrit: taṃ paśyanti mahātmāno brāhmaṇā ye manīṣiṇaḥ dhṛtimanto mahāprājñāḥ sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
english: Him the great-souled brāhmaṇas behold, those who are discerning, steadfast of resolve, of mighty wisdom, devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: evaṃ parimitaṃ kālam ācaran saṃśitavrataḥ āsīno hi rahasy eko gacched akṣarasātmyatām
english: Thus passing the appointed time in observance, firm in his vows, seated alone in a solitary place, he may attain union with the Imperishable.

sanskrit: pramoho bhrama āvarto ghrāṇaśravaṇadarśane adbhutāni rasasparśe śītoṣṇe mārutākṛtiḥ
english: Bewilderment, giddiness, whirling; strange things in smell, hearing, and sight; marvels in taste and touch; sensations of cold and heat, and forms wrought of wind—

sanskrit: pratibhām upasargāṃś cāpy upasaṃgṛhya yogataḥ tāṃs tattvavid anādṛtya svātmanaiva nivartayet
english: such visions and afflictions too may arise through the practice of Yoga; but the knower of truth, disregarding them, should turn them back by his own self.

sanskrit: kuryāt paricayaṃ yoge traikālyaṃ niyato muniḥ giriśṛṅge tathā caitye vṛkṣāgreṣu ca yojajet
english: Self-controlled, the sage should make his practice of Yoga familiar at the three times of day; and he should yoke himself upon a mountain peak, in a sacred shrine, or amid the tops of trees.

sanskrit: saṃniyamyendriyagrāmaṃ goṣṭhe bhāṇḍamanā iva ekāgraś cintayen nityaṃ yogān nodvejayen manaḥ
english: Having reined in the host of the senses, like a herdsman attentive to his vessels in the cow-pen, one-pointed he should meditate ever, and not let the mind grow restless from his Yoga.

sanskrit: yenopāyena śakyeta saṃniyantuṃ calaṃ manaḥ taṃ taṃ yukto niṣeveta na caiva vicalet tataḥ
english: By whatever means the restless mind can be reined in, by that the yoked one should pursue it, and not stray from it thereafter.

sanskrit: śūnyā giriguhāś caiva devatāyatanāni ca śūnyāgārāṇi caikāgro nivāsārtham upakramet
english: Empty mountain caves, the abodes of the gods, and deserted houses—these the one-pointed seeker should resort to for his dwelling.

sanskrit: nābhiṣvajet paraṃ vācā karmaṇā manasāpi vā upekṣako yatāhāro labdhālabdhe samo bhavet
english: He should not cling to another by speech, by deed, or even by thought; indifferent, of measured diet, he should be even-minded toward gain and loss.

sanskrit: yaś cainam abhinandeta yaś cainam apavādayet samas tayoś cāpy ubhayor nābhidhyāyec chubhāśubham
english: Whether one praises him or one reviles him, he should be the same toward both, and should not dwell in thought upon the fair or the foul.

sanskrit: na prahṛṣyeta lābheṣu nālābheṣu ca cintayet samaḥ sarveṣu bhūteṣu sadharmā mātariśvanaḥ
english: He should not exult in gains nor grieve in losses; even-minded toward all beings, he should share the nature of the wind.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarvātmanaḥ sādhoḥ sarvatra samadarśinaḥ ṣaṇmāsān nityayuktasya śabdabrahmātivartate
english: Thus for the holy one, wholly devoted, seeing all things with an equal eye, ever yoked for six months, the Brahman-as-Word is transcended.

sanskrit: vedanārtāḥ prajā dṛṣṭvā samaloṣṭāśmakāñcanaḥ etasmin nirato mārge viramen na vimohitaḥ
english: Beholding mankind tormented with pain, holding a clod, a stone, and gold as equal, devoted to this path, he should not turn back, nor be deluded.

sanskrit: api varṇāv akṛṣṭas tu nārī vā dharmakāṅkṣiṇī tāv apy etena mārgeṇa gacchetāṃ paramāṃ gatim
english: Even those of the lower two classes, untilled by learning, or a woman longing for dharma—even these may by this path attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: ajaṃ purāṇam ajaraṃ sanātanaṃ; yad indriyair upalabhate naro 'calaḥ aṇor aṇīyo mahato mahattaraṃ; tadātmanā paśyati yukta ātmavān
english: The unborn, ancient, ageless, everlasting One, which the unwavering man apprehends through the senses—smaller than the small, greater than the great—that the yoked man, possessed of the Self, beholds by the self.

sanskrit: idaṃ maharṣer vacanaṃ mahātmano; yathāvad uktaṃ manasānudṛśya ca avekṣya ceyāt parameṣṭhisātmyatāṃ; prayānti yāṃ bhūtagatiṃ manīṣiṇaḥ
english: This word of the great-souled mighty sage, duly spoken, having beheld and pondered it in the mind, one should go on to attain union with the Supreme—that goal of beings to which the wise repair.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca yad idaṃ vedavacanaṃ kuru karma tyajeti ca kāṃ diśaṃ vidyayā yānti kāṃ ca gacchanti karmaṇā
english: Śuka said: As for this saying of the Veda—'Perform action' and 'Renounce it'—to what region do men go by knowledge, and to what do they go by action?

sanskrit: etad vai śrotum icchāmi tad bhavān prabravītu me etat tv anyonyavairūpye vartate pratikūlataḥ
english: This I wish to hear; may you declare it to me, for these two stand opposed to each other, each contrary to the other.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ parāśarasutaḥ sutam karmavidyāmayāv etau vyākhyāsyāmi kṣarākṣarau
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, the son of Parāśara replied to his son: 'I shall expound to you these two—the perishable and the imperishable—wrought of action and of knowledge.'

sanskrit: yāṃ diśaṃ vidyayā yānti yāṃ ca gacchanti karmaṇā śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ putra gahvaraṃ hy etad antaram
english: To what region men go by knowledge, and to what they go by action—hear with single-minded attention, my son, for this distinction is a deep and hidden thing.

sanskrit: asti dharma iti proktaṃ nāstīty atraiva yo vadet tasya pakṣasya sadṛśam idaṃ mama bhaved atha
english: 'Dharma exists,' it is declared; and should one say in this same matter 'It exists not'—what I have to say here may seem to match that side as well.

sanskrit: dvāv imāv atha panthānau yatra vedāḥ pratiṣṭhitāḥ pravṛttilakṣaṇo dharmo nivṛttau ca subhāṣitaḥ
english: There are these two paths, on which the Vedas are established: the dharma marked by engagement in action, and that well-praised dharma which lies in withdrawal from it.

sanskrit: karmaṇā badhyate jantur vidyayā tu pramucyate tasmāt karma na kurvanti yatayaḥ pāradarśinaḥ
english: By action the creature is bound, but by knowledge it is set free; therefore the ascetics who see to the far shore perform no action.

sanskrit: karmaṇā jāyate pretya mūrtimān ṣoḍaśātmakaḥ vidyayā jāyate nityam avyayo hy avyayātmakaḥ
english: By action one is born again after death, an embodied being made of the sixteen parts; by knowledge one is born eternal, imperishable, of imperishable nature.

sanskrit: karma tv eke praśaṃsanti svalpabuddhitarā narāḥ tena te dehajālāni ramayanta upāsate
english: Yet some praise action—men of the meaner understanding; thereby they take delight in the webs of bodies and cleave to them.

sanskrit: ye tu buddhiṃ parāṃ prāptā dharmanaipuṇyadarśinaḥ na te karma praśaṃsanti kūpaṃ nadyāṃ pibann iva
english: But those who have attained the higher understanding, who see the subtlety of dharma, do not praise action—as one would not praise a well while drinking at a river.

sanskrit: karmaṇaḥ phalam āpnoti sukhaduḥkhe bhavābhavau vidyayā tad avāpnoti yatra gatvā na śocati
english: From action one reaps fruit—pleasure and pain, birth and rebirth; but by knowledge one attains that whence, having gone, one grieves no more.

sanskrit: yatra gatvā na mriyate yatra gatvā na jāyate na jīryate yatra gatvā yatra gatvā na vardhate
english: That, having reached which one dies not; having reached which one is not born; having reached which one decays not; having reached which one grows no more—

sanskrit: yatra tad brahma paramam avyaktam ajaraṃ dhruvam avyāhatam anāyāsam amṛtaṃ cāviyogi ca
english: that supreme Brahman, unmanifest, ageless, abiding, unobstructed, effortless, deathless, and free from all separation;

sanskrit: dvaṃdvair yatra na bādhyante mānasena ca karmaṇā samāḥ sarvatra maitrāś ca sarvabhūtahite ratāḥ
english: where men are not afflicted by the pairs of opposites, nor by deed of the mind—even-minded toward all, friendly, devoted to the welfare of all beings.

sanskrit: vidyāmayo 'nyaḥ puruṣas tāta karmamayo 'paraḥ viddhi candramasaṃ darśe sūkṣmayā kalayā sthitam
english: One Person, my son, is made of knowledge, and another of action; know it like the moon on the new-moon day, abiding in a single subtle digit.

sanskrit: tad etad ṛṣiṇā proktaṃ vistareṇānumīyate navajaṃ śaśinaṃ dṛṣṭvā vakraṃ tantum ivāmbare
english: This was declared by the seer, and it is inferred at large by beholding the newborn moon, a curved thread in the sky.

sanskrit: ekādaśavikārātmā kalāsaṃbhārasaṃbhṛtaḥ mūrtimān iti taṃ viddhi tāta karmaguṇātmakam
english: Composed of the eleven modifications, built up by the gathering of digits—know that one to be embodied, my son, made of the qualities born of action.

sanskrit: devo yaḥ saṃśritas tasminn abbindur iva puṣkare kṣetrajñaṃ taṃ vijānīyān nityaṃ tyāgajitātmakam
english: The divine One that dwells therein, like a drop of water upon a lotus leaf—know that to be the Knower of the Field, eternal, its nature won through renunciation.

sanskrit: tamo rajaś ca sattvaṃ ca viddhi jīvaguṇān imān jīvam ātmaguṇaṃ vidyād ātmānaṃ paramātmanaḥ
english: Darkness, passion, and purity—know these to be the qualities of the living soul; know the living soul to be a quality of the Self, and the Self a quality of the Supreme Self.

sanskrit: sacetanaṃ jīvaguṇaṃ vadanti; sa ceṣṭate ceṣṭayate ca sarvam tataḥ paraṃ kṣetravido vadanti; prāvartayad yo bhuvanāni sapta
english: They call the living soul, endowed with consciousness, a quality; it stirs and sets all things in motion. Beyond it the knowers of the Field declare that One who set the seven worlds in motion.

sanskrit: śuka uvāca kṣarāt prabhṛti yaḥ sargaḥ saguṇānīndriyāṇi ca buddhyaiśvaryābhisargārthaṃ yad dhyānaṃ cātmanaḥ śubham
english: Śuka said: The creation that proceeds from the perishable, the senses together with the qualities, and the auspicious meditation of the Self that serves the unfolding of intellect and lordly power—

sanskrit: bhūya eva tu loke 'smin sadvṛttiṃ vṛttihaitukīm yayā santaḥ pravartante tad icchāmy anuvarṇitam
english: yet further, here in this world, the right conduct grounded in livelihood, by which the good go forward—that too I wish to have described.

sanskrit: vede vacanam uktaṃ tu kuru karma tyajeti ca katham etad vijānīyāṃ tac ca vyākhyātum arhasi
english: In the Veda the word is spoken, 'Perform action' and 'Renounce it'; how am I to understand this? That too you ought to expound.

sanskrit: lokavṛttāntatattvajñaḥ pūto 'haṃ guruśāsanāt kṛtvā buddhiṃ viyuktātmā tyakṣyāmy ātmānam avyathaḥ
english: Knowing the truth of the world's affairs, made pure by my teacher's instruction, having fixed my resolve, my self detached, I shall lay down this self untroubled.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca yaiṣā vai vihitā vṛttiḥ purastād brahmaṇā svayam eṣā pūrvataraiḥ sadbhir ācīrṇā paramarṣibhiḥ
english: Vyāsa said: This mode of life which was ordained of old by Brahman himself was practiced by the good men of former times, the supreme seers.

sanskrit: brahmacaryeṇa vai lokāñ jayanti paramarṣayaḥ ātmanaś ca hṛdi śreyas tv anviccha manasātmani
english: By the discipline of chastity the supreme seers conquer the worlds; therefore seek the good for your own self within the heart, in the self by the mind.
